description: REGRESSION introduced by the FIND-001/002 fix. The round-1 fix adds a heartbeat SEED on every core (re)start: gig-cli.sh:36 `mkdir -p "$HOME/gig" && touch "$HOME/gig/.last-pass"`. The healthcheck (gig-healthcheck.sh:14) restarts the core via `gig-cli.sh --restart`, which ALWAYS re-runs line 36 and refreshes the heartbeat. The independent auditor's FIRING verdict (the spec's #1 proof, 2026-06-30-gig-earn-core-recipe-design.md:8-11) is derived SOLELY from heartbeat freshness (auditor.sh:35 hb_age, :44 `verdict="FIRING"`). Therefore the self-heal path itself can forge a fresh heartbeat with no real autonomous pass. Concrete failure mode (the author's own documented quota scenario, spec line 17 '96% weekly cap'): if claude cannot run (quota/auth), the detached tmux command exits immediately so the session dies; the launchd healthcheck (every 300s) then restarts it every ~5 min, each restart executing gig-cli.sh:36 and re-seeding the heartbeat. The auditor (launchd :45) reads heartbeat age <5min and writes verdict=FIRING while the core has completed ZERO real gig passes. The 'independent proof that the loop self-runs' is thus produced by the restart mechanism, not by work. Pre-fix (round 1, no seed) the heartbeat would have aged out and the auditor honestly reported STALE/DEAD; the fix decoupled 'heartbeat fresh' from 'a real pass happened'.

evidence.snippet:
tmux -S "$SOCK" new-session -d -s "$SESSION" -c "$HOME" "$CLAUDE" ... -- "$STARTUP"
mkdir -p "$HOME/gig" && touch "$HOME/gig/.last-pass"   # FIND-001/002: seed the heartbeat clock at startup

fix: Separate the liveness seed from the work heartbeat. Seed a distinct file (e.g. ~/gig/.last-start) at startup; let ONLY a completed cron pass touch ~/gig/.last-pass. The auditor's FIRING verdict must require a .last-pass that was NOT written by a restart. Alternatively require the auditor to also confirm applied.jsonl/actions_total advanced before emitting FIRING (heartbeat freshness alone must not yield FIRING).
